projects.name: AI Software Factory
projects.category: AI Product Engineering · Agentic Software Development
projects.description: An AI-native approach to software product development — an orchestration platform that turns product requirements into implementation-ready software changes through specifications, specialist agents and engineering workflows.
projects.tagline: An AI-native approach to software product development.

caseStudy.problem: Bridging the gap between product requirements and high-quality implementation changes — reducing the friction, inconsistency and review overhead that slow down AI-assisted development.
caseStudy.product: An orchestration platform that turns a business requirement into a specification, plans the work, dispatches specialist agents, and produces an implementation-ready change through validation and pull requests.
caseStudy.architecture: A pipeline from requirement intake to specification, planning, specialist-agent dispatch, implementation, validation and pull request — coordinated by agent orchestration, with context engineering and git-based workflows.
caseStudy.decisions: Specification as the source of truth; specialist agents over a single monolithic agent; automated review and validation gates; git and pull requests as the collaboration interface.
caseStudy.challenges: Keeping generated changes consistent, giving each agent the right context, and maintaining quality through automated validation.
caseStudy.tradeoffs: Balancing agent autonomy against validation rigor, context size against relevance, and generation speed against correctness.

projects.name: MARK1 — AI Technical Support Agent
projects.description: An AI agent that investigates technical support requests end to end — turning scattered documentation, support tickets and legacy source code into grounded technical answers.
projects.tagline: An agentic workflow that investigates support requests across documentation, tickets and code.

caseStudy.problem: Technical support in enterprise software requires investigating scattered documentation, historical tickets and legacy code — a slow, knowledge-intensive process that rarely has a single obvious answer.
caseStudy.product: An AI technical support agent that investigates a request end to end, combining retrieval across documentation, tickets and codebase with dependency analysis to produce a grounded technical answer.
caseStudy.architecture: An agent orchestrator built with LangGraph coordinates hybrid retrieval (BM25 + vector search) over documentation, tickets and code, performs code and dependency analysis, and produces a grounded LLM response — with evaluation and observability.
caseStudy.decisions: Agent orchestration via LangGraph; hybrid retrieval (BM25 + vector) instead of a single retrieval path; dependency analysis to understand code relationships; grounding answers in retrieved evidence.
caseStudy.challenges: Retrieval quality across heterogeneous sources, grounding to avoid hallucination, and understanding legacy code dependencies.
caseStudy.tradeoffs: Retrieval latency versus answer quality; hybrid search coverage versus index complexity; agent autonomy versus control.

projects.name: Luna — Enterprise AI Knowledge Platform
projects.description: A multi-tenant AI platform that turns organizational knowledge into context-aware AI capabilities — connecting documents, meetings, incidents and systems into grounded, governed answers.
projects.tagline: Product architecture / platform concept / ongoing development

caseStudy.problem: Organizational knowledge is fragmented across documents, meetings, incidents, APIs and integrations, and cannot be turned into reliable AI capabilities at enterprise scale.
caseStudy.product: A multi-tenant platform that consolidates organizational knowledge into a knowledge layer, grounds it with RAG, exposes it through agents, and delivers it to business applications.
caseStudy.architecture: Multiple ingestion sources feed a knowledge layer with Qdrant-based retrieval and LangGraph agents, governed by multi-tenancy, observability, governance and privacy-by-design (LGPD), and exposed through integrations to business applications.
caseStudy.decisions: Multi-tenancy as a first-class concern; a knowledge layer abstraction; RAG for grounded retrieval; governance and privacy-by-design (LGPD) from the start.
caseStudy.challenges: Isolating tenants, governing data, and balancing retrieval quality with governance and privacy requirements.
caseStudy.tradeoffs: RAG fidelity versus complexity; governance overhead versus speed; multi-tenant isolation versus operational cost.

projects.name: SpecKitBasic
projects.description: A lightweight specification-driven approach that gives AI coding agents structured context, rules and a single source of truth — the foundation behind the AI Software Factory orchestration.
projects.tagline: A lightweight specification-driven approach to AI-assisted development.

caseStudy.problem: AI-assisted development becomes unpredictable without a clear, structured source of truth for what should be built.
caseStudy.product: A lean workflow where a requirement becomes a specification, drives an architecture/plan, and guides implementation and validation — the lightweight foundation the AI Software Factory builds on.
caseStudy.architecture: A minimal pipeline from requirement to specification to plan to implementation to validation, focused on structured context and rules rather than heavy tooling.
caseStudy.decisions: Specification as the source of truth; lightweight rules; structured requirements; prioritizing consistency over breadth of automation.
caseStudy.challenges: Managing context efficiently and keeping requirements structured enough for reliable AI-assisted development.
caseStudy.tradeoffs: Simplicity versus capability; structure versus speed of iteration.

projects.name: Enterprise MCP Platform
projects.description: An exploration of how enterprise systems can safely become usable by AI agents — a platform concept for exposing enterprise APIs and capabilities through MCP with security, governance and access control.

caseStudy.problem: AI agents need access to enterprise capabilities, but exposing APIs directly creates security, access-control and governance risk.
caseStudy.product: A platform that abstracts enterprise APIs and capabilities behind MCP, so AI agents can be enabled safely and consistently.
caseStudy.architecture: Enterprise APIs are exposed through an MCP layer with security, governance and access control, then consumed by AI agents.
caseStudy.decisions: MCP as the standard interface; API abstraction; access control and governance as platform capabilities; enabling agents without direct API exposure.
caseStudy.challenges: Securing agent access, governing data, and keeping integrations consistent across the enterprise.
caseStudy.tradeoffs: Security rigor versus agent flexibility; abstraction versus integration fidelity.

thinking.title: How I think about AI
thinking.intro: The questions I work through when designing an AI product.

tensions.title: Agent or deterministic workflow?
tensions.body: Not every problem needs an agent. I start from the workflow and introduce an agent only when autonomy, tool use or multi-step reasoning genuinely creates value.

tensions.title: RAG or structured data?
tensions.body: The retrieval architecture follows the information problem — grounded questions need retrieval; well-defined queries may not need it at all.

tensions.title: Bigger model or better context?
tensions.body: I optimize the whole system — prompts, context, retrieval and flow — before reaching for a larger model.

tensions.title: Accuracy, latency or cost?
tensions.body: AI product decisions are product decisions. The right trade-off depends on the experience, the risk and the business value at stake.

tensions.title: Human or AI?
tensions.body: Human-in-the-loop stays wherever the business risk requires it — for review, judgment and accountability.

thinking.diagramCaption: I evaluate AI product decisions as product trade-offs, not purely technical decisions.

approach.title: How I build AI products
approach.message: AI products are not built by choosing an LLM first. They are built by understanding the problem, designing the right experience, choosing the appropriate AI architecture, validating quality and measuring product impact.

experience.title: Engineering background. Product mindset.
experience.body: Years of software engineering experience gave me the technical foundation to understand complex systems. Product management added the ability to frame problems, prioritize outcomes and connect engineering decisions to business value.
experience.body2: My background in enterprise software gives me a practical perspective on introducing AI into complex, legacy environments — where data quality, integrations, reliability, governance and business constraints matter.
